_about: Keys, keyholes and locked doors, decoded from android_game.bin. Where the Godot project's
data/actors.json guesses a different number it is carried beside as
ONE range, used twice. The key's init writes squaredRange = scale(26)^2, and that same
value is the test for being picked up and the test for opening a keyhole. actors.json
invents two separate ranges, pickup_range_px and unlock_range_px, and guesses 40 for
Pickup is a distance poll, not a contact - the key scans the entities around it every
frame. actors.json says the same, and it is right: there is no contact callback for a
key anywhere in the binary. Anything that isCharacter OR isMinion can take one, so a
unlocked is ONE-WAY. The string appears exactly twice in the whole binary: the key sets
it, the keyhole reads it. Nothing re-locks a door.
Colour is an explicit metadata/color string on all three roles and is absent from none
of them in any of the 128 levels. 41 keyhole/door pairs, averaging 75 px apart, the

_note: A carried key trails its owner through an interpolator rather than being placed on
it: followUp re-aims every 20 ms and interpolates each aim over 60, so the key sits
perpetually behind whoever holds it. Beyond leash_px it is slammed onto the owner by
forceFollowUpPosition, which is also what carries it through a portal.
The original eases with a smoothEnd filter; the port blends linearly between aims.
Nothing in the carry path touches velocity, which is why a key is state with a
position here rather than a body: key.ent is density 0 with no custom data but color.
_carrier_point: measures the pickup from the carrier's GetPositionXY (ins 744-753, squaredDistance against
squaredRange) and leads the key to that same GetPositionXY (ins 932-957 the scale(40)
leash and forceFollowUpPosition, 959-976 followUp): the carrier's ENTITY point, not the
centre of whatever body the port gives it. A minion's entity point stands
minions.json body.entity_above_feet_px (18.1) over its feet, which is 11.1 over the
port's body centre, so Game offers each minion to the keys at that point (Carry::Carrier)
and a key a knight carries rides at its chest, drawn behind it (the keys are placed at
eth_z 0 or below, the minion at world 2). The player is offered at its capsule's centre,
18.1 over its feet since step 153, the original's (dark_mage.ent's compound is minion.ent's):
the same point as a minion's entity point, so there is no deviation left to apply here.

_note: An unlocked keyhole holds still for fade_start_ms, fades its alpha to nothing over
fade_ms, and then deletes BOTH its door and itself. The door is the only one of the
three the player can collide with - door_locked.ent is shape=1, static=1, 30 x 126 -
so that deletion is the whole of what unlocking does to a level.

_source: THE RED KEY'S OWN LIGHT (CMP-7, planning step 168). Decoded from ETHCallback_key (Enhanced's
out/parity/asbc/all_functions.txt, md5 48fe65ce8baea16b94ed84d8d7be84b0, L90381, bytes
438490..442683). A call pushes its last argument first (00_order 8.0 rule 3):
#119-142 GetString('color') == 'red': opEquals, and JLowZ #142 jumps to #187 when it is not;
#144-149 && !IsHidden(): NOT, and JLowZ #149 jumps to #187 likewise;
#151-156 scale = GetScale().x;
#158-186 AddLight(GetPosition() + vector3(0, 0, 6 x scale), vector3(1, 0, 0), 48 x scale, 0):
#158-159 the bool (SetV1 0), #160-161 the range MULIf 48, #162-166 the colour pushed 0, 0, 1f
so x = 1 (red; read the other way it would be a blue light on a red key), #168-173 the offset
pushed 6 x scale, 0, 0 so z = 6 x scale, #175-185 GetPosition() + that, #186 AddLight.
Planning step 69's prose said the offset was (6 x scale, 0, 0), an x offset: the push
order says z, and the colour's, read the same way, is red.
The two jumps skip only that block and rejoin at #187: the light is added on EVERY call, before
the foundKeyhole branch (#204-220, the fly-in, which ends in DeleteEntity at #646) and the
ownerID branch (#653-665, a carried key), and before linearMotion (#666-679) and the carry's moves
(#932-976) of the same call. So a key lying, carried or flying into its keyhole is lit, and no
line of the callback hides a key: the light follows a carried key (its GetPosition() is where the
last call left it, so the light stands one frame behind the picture) and goes with the key.
The engine: ETHScriptWrapper::AddLight (ETHScriptWrapper.Drawing.cpp:171-183) makes ETHLight(true)
with castShadows, colour, pos and range as given and staticLight false, and ETHScene::AddLight
(ETHScene.cpp:792-795) hands it to ETHEntityRenderingManager::AddLight (ETHEntityRenderingManager.cpp:
161-172), which keeps it unless its colour is black or it is off the screen: it is NOT scaled by an
owner (BuildChildLight, :174-184, is for a light an entity owns) and NOT multiplied by
ComputeLightIntensity (:111-114, the owner's live particle share), so the sparkles of key.ent do
not dim it. The shader multiplies every light's colour by the scene's lightIntensity
(ETHPixelLightDiffuseSpecular.cpp:146), and a light that is not static reaches static sprites
(ETHEntitySpriteRenderer.cpp:70).
UNITS. Game::preLoop #37 runs SGlobalScale::scaleEntities: scaleEntity (bytes 6072..6337) #30-36
Scale(getScale() x individualScale) and #38-53 SetPosition(GetPosition() x getScale()), the z
included. A key places no 'scale' datum and key.ent's <Scale> is (1, 1), so GetScale().x is
getScale() and both numbers are in the screen's pixels: 48 x getScale() range and a z of 6 x
getScale() over the key's own scaled z. The port's units are the level's, a screen's pixels over
getScale() (a torch's 300-unit range is drawn 300 units wide, test_mp_layer), so the range is 48
units and the height 6 units over the key node's eth_z, which Look::z is.
HIDDEN. #64-88 of SGlobalScale::scaleEntities hide an entity that carries the 'hidden' datum, the
one way a key is hidden. Of the original's 133 scenes (reference/extracted/assets/scenes, read as
UTF-16) none contains the word 'hidden'; hide="0" appears only in level_select0-3 and
loading_screen, and no key entity has hide="1" (39 keys, 133 scenes): no level places a hidden
key, so the port does not read it. Only two keys are red, level18c's key_2701 (4-19, z -2) and
level19c's key_1335 (4-20, z -6); the keys the Ghost and the Dark Dragon drop are yellow
(ghost.json, darkdragon.json key_colour).
_deviation: A key that has found its keyhole flies into it and is deleted at the fly-in's last frame (#646):
the port draws that since planning step 233 (effects.json key_fly_in, Effects::PoseOf), so the key's
picture, its sparkles and this light go on that frame, about 1.3 s after the unlock and before the
keyhole (1.5 s). The light is tied to the picture, so it ends with it. A key the layer cannot find the
fly-in's clock for is still held where it opened its keyhole until that keyhole is gone.

_note: By COLOUR, never by proximity. The original matches a keyhole or a door by name
(both spellings, keyhole and keyhole.ent) and then compares its color string against
the key's own.
For the door a keyhole opens, the original uses seekNeighbourEntity over a 3x3 block
of buckets, centre first, and falls back to a global seekEntity when that finds
nothing - so the bucket walk is an optimisation and not a rule. The port takes the
nearest door of the keyhole's colour in the level, which gives the same answer
everywhere: level20b is the only level holding two pairs of one colour, and there
each keyhole is 57 px from its own door and 216 px or more from the other.
The bucket SIZE is set from script - 128 of the level's units, red_key_state.bucket_units
below (planning step 118, fix round 1; this note said otherwise until then). It does not
change the port's answer here: the key's search is bounded by the 26 px test rather than
by the buckets, and the door's has the global fallback.

_measured: Footage F17 (out/parity/footage/F17.md section 2.4, 4-19 take r5): the stone row's grey
level fits L0 x smoothBeginning(smoothEnd(1 - (t - t0) / 6)) with t0 7.573 s and RMS 0.59
grey levels over 66 frames (#140-#205), t0 0.12 s after the teleport that took the key
after t0 against the decoded 6000 ms at that take's 13.5-18.8 fps. Lit sprites go black
and emissive ones stay (the ambient term min(1, ambient + emissive)).
_bucket_units: GetBucket is floor(position / bucketSize) (Ethanon ETHBucketManager.cpp:47-50). Game::start
(listing L21003) #3-17 builds vector2(128, 128) x g_scale.getScale() and pushes it FIRST, so
it is the last argument; #44-48 push four strings more, and #49 is the only five-argument
LoadScene (string x4, vector2; ETHScriptWrapper.generic.cpp:316), which hands the scene
v2BucketSize x the engine's own scale (ETHScriptWrapper.Scene.cpp:637-642) - 1.0, as nothing
sets it (00_order 8.0 rule 5). Game::preLoop #37 then runs SGlobalScale::scaleEntities, which
scales every entity without scalable = 0 (bytes 6838..7228 #13-50; level18c marks none):
scaleEntity (bytes 6072..6337 #38-53) SetPosition(GetPosition() x getScale()). Both see one
256 before any level state runs Game::start, and the scene's preLoop (L61752 #1-4) sets it
again before Game::preLoop. So a bucket is 128 x f screen pixels over positions x f: 128 of
the level's units whatever the screen (360 px at 720). On level18c the state, its key and
breakable_wall_2756 all stand in bucket (3, 1), x 384-512, y 128-256; the state's y 128 is
that row's top edge. Planning step 118's first reading, the four-string LoadScene and
Ethanon's default 256 px = 91.02 units, was wrong (its fix round 1).

_counts_not_matching_the_remake: actors.json says the colour multisets are identical per level, per role. Counted over
all 128 levels they are not: 39 keys against 41 keyholes and 41 doors. Four levels
disagree - level0c and level31b and level31c each hold a keyhole and a door with no
key, and level18c holds a red key with no keyhole and no door.
level18c's is explained since planning step 118: its lock is a wall, not a door. The
red_key_state block above breaks breakable_wall_2756 6000 ms after the red key is taken.
level31b's and level31c's keys are the bosses' drops (Ghost, DarkDragon). The red key's
help popup (ui.json) and its achievement 61 are not decoded here.
_not_built: The fly-in animation a spent key plays (a WaypointManager of timed waypoints with smoothEnd
filters that carries the key from where it was into the keyhole) is BUILT since planning step
233: effects.json key_fly_in has its six waypoints, Effects::AdvanceFlyIn its clock and
Effects::PoseOf where the key stands on it; the layer draws the key there. This file's state
(`spent`, `opened`, the keyhole's own clock) is unchanged by it.
Still not built: fixKeyAngle (the -45 degree tilt of a carried key; the flight's first leg turns
the key from 0, not from -45, to -90). (The sounds that went with it, in the line this replaces, are
sounds.json's since; the red key's achievement 61 is the achievements module's, not this file's.)
(The red key's per-frame AddLight is built since planning step 168: red_light above.
The earthquake a door's removal starts is built since step 101: earthquake.json's
door_unlocked, fired from `opened`. The five effect
entities - key_pick.ent where a key is taken, key_unlock_halo.ent on the fly-in's frame
1, and wall_destroy.ent, door_locked_vanish.ent and keyhole_vanish.ent where the
keyhole goes - are drawn since step 107, from effects.json _keys: the layer reads
`owner`, `spent`/`opened` and a keyhole's `gone`, and the fly-in's clock is
Effects::AdvanceFlyIn, not this file's. The idle bob is step 69's, motions.json.)
setKeyColor, which repaints a blue or red key, keyhole or locked door by swapping its
sprite to <entityName>_blue.png or _red.png, is drawn since planning step 120, from the
port's art.json key_colour: a picture, not this file's. Yellow is the base art and is
never repainted, which is why yellow dominates every count above.
